name: starter:slate

req.title: Find companies hiring in a market and put candidates in front of them
req.summary: Find companies hiring in an industry and area, build a candidate slate for each, and run the Arena 5x5.

vals.ai_fallback: Have DripDrop's AI build the rest
vals.who_to_reach: owners and C-level first, then VPs, then directors, then managers, with HR and talent acquisition last
vals.newsletter_mode: Find the one that fits, skip it if none does
vals.boards: Google Jobs first, then ZipRecruiter, then LinkedIn
vals.unattended: Stop and check with me first

prompt:
I need you to do this for me, using my DripDrop connector.

WHAT I WANT
  Find companies hiring in an industry and area, build a candidate slate for
  each, and run the Arena 5x5.

THE DETAILS
  How many candidates to put in front of each company: 3
  If the Pipeline comes up short: Have DripDrop's AI build the rest
  How big a company: 50 to 1000 people
  Who to reach: owners and C-level first, then VPs, then directors, then
  managers, with HR and talent acquisition last

I HAVEN'T DECIDED THESE
  What kind of company
  Where
  What jobs they're hiring for
  Ask me about all of them in one go before you start, not one at a time as
  you hit them.

HOW TO DO IT
  1. Search the job boards for companies hiring <what jobs they're hiring
     for> in <where>, posted in the last 30 days. Google Jobs first, then
     ZipRecruiter, then LinkedIn. If Google shows a bot check, do not try to
     solve it: drop to ZipRecruiter and tell me Google was skipped. Run
     ZipRecruiter either way.
  2. Take these out before you go any further: anything someone on my team
     has already worked; companies we already do business with; other
     recruiters, staffing firms, job boards and government listings. Tell me
     how many you dropped and why.
  3. Size about 12 companies to land 5 of about 50 to 1000 people, and name
     3 ranked reserves. For every pick give the concrete signal that earned
     it, the actual fact from the posting, not "good fit". For every reserve
     give its demerit.
  4. Now build the slate. For each company, search the DripDrop Pipeline
     with candidates_search for 3 people who genuinely fit the openings you
     found there. Use a limit of 1 or 2 per query - the full resume text is
     large and a wide query will blow the context. Score each one against
     the actual posting and say what the evidence was. The same title is not
     the same job.
  5. If a company comes up short - fewer than 3 real people in the Pipeline
     who actually fit - do not drop the company and do not pad the slate
     with someone who does not fit. Fill the gap the way DripDrop's own
     Create profiles with AI step does: write each missing one as an
     anonymous sample profile built from the job title and what the posting
     is asking for - the right level, the focus, the certifications - and
     label them Candidate A, Candidate B, Candidate C in order. Never give a
     sample profile a real person's name or employer. In your read-back, say
     for every company which slots are real bench people and which are
     AI-built samples.
  6. Pull the buying centre for each company out of ZoomInfo. Aim for 7
     contacts per company; 3 is the floor that qualifies a company at all,
     15 is the cap. Work down owners and C-level first, then VPs, then
     directors, then managers, with HR and talent acquisition last.
  7. Show me the companies, the slate you built for each, the contacts and
     the total send volume. This run must not send more than 175 emails - if
     it would, cut the weakest companies until it doesn't. Then stop and
     wait for me to say go.
  8. Once I say go, build one campaign per company with create_campaign
     using template "fivebyfive", start_date "auto", which the server
     resolves to the upcoming Monday, and industry, location and roles set
     from THE DETAILS above. Pass that company's 3 people in the candidates
     argument, one card each, shaped {"label": "Candidate A", "role": a real
     job title, "bullets": three bullets} - and each bullet is a skillset, a
     notable project, or a company they have worked for. No
     years-of-experience, location or salary bullets. Do not use their names
     or their current employers anywhere in the outreach. Describe them by
     what they have actually done. Name each campaign after the company
     name. Newsletter: run campaigns_list first and look at my evergreen
     newsletters — the ongoing ones, usually named for a trade or an
     industry, sometimes with an area in the name too. Match on the line of
     work, not the map: a manufacturing newsletter is the right home for a
     manufacturing campaign and a construction one for a construction
     campaign, and the area in the name does not have to match — I keep
     broad ones for exactly this. Pass that newsletter's exact name as the
     enroll_newsletter argument. Only if nothing on the list is in the same
     line of work, leave enroll_newsletter off entirely: do not create a
     newsletter. Tell me which one you used, or that there wasn't one. Read
     back the campaign id, the step count, the queued-contact count and
     which slate went out for every one, and tell me about any that came
     back short.

TOOLS
  Use my DripDrop connector: candidates_search, campaign_types,
  my_campaign_styles, campaigns_list, create_campaign. If a tool is missing
  or returns an auth error then the connector is not connected — stop and
  tell me, do not work around it.

HOW I WANT YOU TO WORK
  - Show me what you have before anything sends, imports or spends credits,
    and wait for me to say go.
  - If a step is blocked, quote the literal error and tell me what you could
    not determine. Do not guess at a cause and do not pad around it.
  - Do not invent a specific. Every company, number and date you give me has
    to come from something you actually read.


If any of this is ambiguous, ask me before you start rather than after.

prompt:
I need you to do this for me.

WHAT I WANT
  Work every LinkedIn card on Today's Tasks and send each person the
  connection request DripDrop wrote for them.

THE DETAILS
  Which LinkedIn tasks: Everything due today, plus anything overdue
  The connection note: Use the message DripDrop shows, word for word
  If you're already connected to them: Skip them and mark the task done

HOW TO DO IT
  1. Open dripdripdrop.ai in the browser and go to Today's Tasks. If it asks
     you to sign in, stop and tell me - do not try to work around the login.
  2. Read every LinkedIn card on that page. Take today's and the ones
     flagged OVERDUE both. Each card gives you the person's name, their
     title and company, a link to their LinkedIn profile, and the connection
     message DripDrop wrote for that campaign. Collect all of them before
     you send anything.
  3. Tell me how many you found and which campaigns they came from, then
     carry on without waiting for me - flag anything that looks wrong as you
     go.
  4. Then work them one at a time. Open the person's profile from the link
     on their card, send a connection request, and attach the note. Send
     DripDrop's message exactly as it appears on the card - it is already
     written for that campaign and already inside LinkedIn's 300-character
     limit. Do not reword it, do not add to it, and do not swap in a name
     the card does not show.
  5. If you are already connected to someone, there is nothing to send: mark
     that task done in DripDrop and move on. List every one you handled this
     way.
  6. Stop at 25 requests in this run even if there are more cards left, and
     stop immediately if LinkedIn shows you any limit or restriction warning
     - quote it to me word for word if it does. Do not retry a request
     LinkedIn refused.
  7. After each request actually goes through, go back to the DripDrop tab
     and mark that person's task done with the Done button on their row.
     Mark it only once the request has genuinely sent - a task ticked off
     for a request that never went is worse than one left open, because
     nothing will bring it back.
  8. Do not send a request to anyone whose card you could not actually read,
     and do not guess a profile URL from a name. If a card has no LinkedIn
     link, skip it and list it for me.
  9. When you finish, tell me how many requests went out, how many you
     skipped and the reason for each, and how many cards are still waiting.

HOW I WANT YOU TO WORK
  - Run this start to finish without stopping to ask. Nobody is watching.
    Log every judgement call you made so I can read them afterwards, and
    stop only if you would otherwise have to invent something.
  - If a step is blocked, quote the literal error and tell me what you could
    not determine. Do not guess at a cause and do not pad around it.
  - Do not invent a specific. Every company, number and date you give me has
    to come from something you actually read.

THEN MAKE IT REPEAT
  Run this again every weekday at 8:00am Mountain time, and keep running it
  on that schedule.
  Create the recurring task with this whole brief baked into it, filled in
  with everything above, so a scheduled run needs nothing from me. Read the
  name and the schedule back to me once you have made it.


If any of this is ambiguous, ask me before you start rather than after.
